Thank you for supporting me through it all 🫶🏾.  As we welcome 2023 from our new home in San Francisco I couldn’t be further (emotionally and literally 😅) from the person I was.  Scary…AND freeing 🤍. caption: Last year I was fortunate enough to visit the @maisonmargiela atelier in Paris before it closed down. The building, a former convent in the 11th, I knew by heart from documentaries and books. Furniture covered in white fabric, white paint splatter everywhere from when Martin and his team first moved in.  This season I was invited to the House’s new (and much bigger) HQ in the 16th. It may not have Martin’s soul, but his legacy lives on. It’s in the white fabric covered chairs at the reception, the tabi shaped footprints directing to the elevators, his bottle lamps with blank labels.  But the new HQ also has John Galliano written all over it. To celebrate the move, the basement atelier was turned into an art installation inspired by his short film for the latest Artisanal collection called Cinema Inferno. Thanks so much for showing me around @moakarlsvard and for letting me drool over the AW23 collection (and for bombarding you with questions about what it’s like to work for MM as the fashion nerd I am)

caption: From planting trees, regenerating springs and depleted soils, and protecting turtles, jaguars … everything impacts nature. The power of nature comes from its diversity, and it depends on it for survival.  Every form of life uniquely creates balance on Earth so all of life can flourish. Cada forma de vida desempenha um papel especial no equilíbrio da Terra, possibilitando que todas as formas de vida possam prosperar. Assim como acontece com as pessoas, nossas diferenças também são nossos pontos fortes, e ficamos mais fortes quando trabalhamos juntos. De norte a sul, de leste a oeste, selecionamos 7 projetos em diferentes regiões do país porque sabemos da importância que cada bioma tem no todo, pois tudo está interligado.  Agora, juntamente com @brazilfound, no dia 20 de maio, em Miami, teremos um jantar para arrecadar mais fundos para que possamos ampliar nossos esforços e ter um impacto ainda maior.

caption: #SaoPaulo 🇧🇷 the first #brutalist house created by Brazilian #architect Paulo Mendes da Rocha is now home to an artist residency program: @domo.damo (“house of love” in Esperanto): a hybrid-home-secret  I got to meet the three artists who are currently spending three months living/creating in this intimate and monumental place:  Congolese painter and poet Merveille KéléKélé @merveillekelekelekelekelelele who is studying Fine Arts at Beaux-arts of Paris. “I write poetry all the time, it’s like a vital need for me and based on my texts, I make paintings.”  Brasília-based visual artist Poli Pieratti @polipieratti “My paintings are compositions based on bodily impressions that memories activate – in general, I give more light and add water and fluidity to what was experienced, in an attempt to pacify the past. I map out new paths for memories, fertilizing dry narratives and adding water to the land of dreams.”  Brazilian sculptor, dancer and performer Luana Vitra @cadeiadecorpo  What’s the story of the house? In 1962, Italian artist and gallery owner Gaetano Miano commissioned da Rocha to build his residence where the Miano’s only lived between 1964 and 1968, when the family left for Rome to escape Brazil’s military dictatorship.  Recently, Parisian art gallerist Benjamin Trigano, the founder of Los Angeles apartment-concept gallery M+B and #SP-based French entrepreneur David Laloum came across the residence and decided to make it an art project.  #PauloMendesdaRocha (1928 – 2021) was one of the essential names of the #EscolaPaulista (#PaulistaSchool), an informal group of Brazilian architects who popularised brutalism, embracing exposed concrete structures, chunkier massing, and rougher finishes - as opposed to the smoother curvy surfaces of the Carioca School, à la Oscar Niemeyer.  #DomoDamo #BrazilianBrutalism #arquitetura #arquiteturabrasileira #brutalistarchitecture #SaoPauloBrutalism #archi #arch #architecture #archidaily #archilovers #archilover #archiporn #Brasil #Brazil #FacehunterSP

caption: #Brutalism in #BuenosAires 🇦🇷  While #Argentina’s capital is known for its French neoclassical, neo-gothic, Beaux-Arts, art nouveau, art deco and modern #architecture, brutalism has also left its discreet but impactful mark.  Three Argentinian #concrete landmarks:   1-4: Biblioteca Nacional Mariano Moreno, designed in 1961 by Italo-Argentine #architect Clorindo Manuel José Testa (1923-2013), in partnership with Francisco Bullrich (1929-2011) and Alicia Cazzaniga (1928-1968). Its construction started in 1971 but successive changes in government leadership, complex bureaucracy and certain indifference towards culture matters by some leaders slowed down the process a lot and the National Library was finally inaugurated in 1992. The location is rich in significance as the concrete building stands on the exact site where President Juan Perón and his wife Eva Duarte (“Evita”) had their official residence: the Unzué Palace. They were initially (1946-1952) highly popular among working class but from 1952, things got complicated and Evita passed away. Juan Perón would eventually lose its power in a military coup and be forced to leave the country. Their residence would symbolically be destroyed in 1958.  5-7: Banca de Londres, designed by Clorindo Testa and built in 1966 as the HQ of the Bank of London and South America, a British bank that would later on be merged with Lloyds.  8-9: Brazilian Embassy’s Chancellery by Olavo Redig Do Campos (1906-1984). The Brazilian architect was president of the Brazilian Heritage Conservation Service of the Foreign Ministry between 1946 and 1976. This privileged position allowed him to design several state buildings outside Brazil such as embassies in Washington DC, Lima, diplomatic residences in Beirut, Dakar and more...  #archi #arch #archilovers #arquitectura #arquitecturaargentina #buenosairesarquitectura #brutalismo #architecturephotography #concretedesign #arquitecturabrutalista #brutalist #brutalistarchitecture #archidaily #archiporn #archilovers #BsAs #Travel #travelling #travelgram #FacehunterBA

caption: #Christianity in #Baghdad 🇮🇶 I didn’t  expect to see so many #churches in town.  There are nowadays about 250,000 Christians left in #Iraq. Until the Gulf War in 1991, they used to be 1-1,5 million. Years of wars and persecution made their number fall drastically. While many fled abroad, some of them moved to the nation's capital to find refuge. #Baghdad is home to some of the largest Christian populations in the country.  The #Christians of Iraq are considered to be one of the world’s oldest continuous Christian communities. Actually, most of them are not Arabs, they are mainly Assyrian people - even though during the Saddam regime, they were pressured to identify as Arabs. Many of them still speak Assyrian as a first language.  I asked Raya @kamelea_roze a pharmacy major student and musician  how is it to live in Baghdad as a Christian in 2023.  “I’m a Chaldean Catholic, I used to be the choir’s pianist in my church (St. George) for five years, and also played piano at several other churches.   I haven’t faced any difficulties or discrimination due to my religion. I believe that religious differences don’t create barriers between people anymore. It may have happened in the past, but it is over now. Which is something I am glad about. I think all Iraqi people, regardless of religion and beliefs, aim to live peacefully and calmly. Despite all the terror that us christians faced in the past, in addition to other Iraqi sects who went through similar experiences. I believe all of us are facing the same fate, since we live in the same country.”  Two thirds of Christians in Iraq are Chaldean Catholics and 20% belong to the Assyrian Church of the East.  Smaller denominations include Syrian Orthodox, Syriac Catholic, Armenian Catholic, Armenian Orthodox, Anglican, Evangelical and other Protestants.  Photo 9: Bakram, in front of an Armenian church: “There are 345 Armenian families in Iraq, we have been living here for centuries and still speak Armenian.”  #iraqichristians #baghdad_iraq #travel #travelphotography #travelling  #FacehunterIraq

caption: #Baghdad 🇮🇶 #LeCorbusier‘s most mysterious project?  The destiny of Baghdad Gymnasium is fascinating.  1. it’s almost a miracle that it actually exists 2. for many years, its existence fell into obscurity in the architecture world 3. Le Corbusier’s paternity remained controversial for quite some time  In 1957, eight of the most important Western architects: Le Corbusier, Walter Gropius, José Luis Sert, Gio Ponti, Aalvar Aalto and Werner March Constantine Doxiadis were commissioned by King Faisal II to transform Baghdad into a modern and cosmopolitan capital.  Le Corbusier was originally hired to create Baghdad Stadium and City of Sport in support of the city's bid to host the 1960 Olympics.  On July 14th 1958, just one day after the project was formally approved, a coup d’état ended the 37-year Hashemite monarchy of Iraq and the king was assassinated. Most of the large-scale projects imagined by the starchitects were instantly abandoned.  As the Iraqi capital didn't get the Olympic Games, the construction of the complex was postponed. Le Corbusier's passed away in 1965.  Thanks to the support of influential Iraqi #architect Rifat Chadirji, a part of the sports city, with -reportedly- little modification to the original plans - would eventually be built under the supervision of French architect Axel Mesney between 1978 and 1980 and inaugurated under the name: Saddam Hussein Gymnasium.  For decades, it suffered from the plight of being a posthumous work. Contested by the #architecture purists, it was never mentionned in the literature dedicated to the Swiss-born French architect. It was perceived as a 'bastardized project', not bearing the master’s signature.   While researching for her thesis on modern architecture in Baghdad, in 2004, researcher Caecilia Pieri got interested in the complex. After years of research, in 2012, she managed to put a hand on never-seen-before construction archives at Axel Mesney’s proving Le Corbusier’s authorship.  The site was renovated a decade ago and is now fully functional. It is mainly used for basketball and volleyball games.  #FacehunterIraq #modernistarchitecture #brutalist #brutalistarchitecture #concrete #archi #arch

caption: #Baghdad 🇮🇶 Burj Abboud, 1955, by #RifatChadirji (1926-2020) and Abdullah Ihsan Kamil (1919-1984)  This Bauhaus-influenced tower represents the symbol of Baghdad intense modernisation and westernisation in the 1950s. It was back then the first high-rise in town.  While the #AbboudBuilding includes some vernacular features such as archways, screens, and courtyards in response to the hot environment, it remains mainly a project borrowing to the “International Style”, built at a time when Chadirji was employed by the monarchy -mandated under British rule.  It’s really in the 1960s, in a post-monarchy republic, that the “father of  #Iraqi modernism” will fully express his unique style that he called “international regionalism”. The idea was to “combine ancient Iraqi heritage with modern art and architecture, to develop an Iraqi aesthetic, that was not only unique to Iraq, but also influence the development of a pan-Arab visual language”.  With nearly 100 buildings, Chadirji contributed greatly to define the aesthetics of his country’s public space, especially through the 1970s. By 1970 Chadirji had offices throughout the Middle East, one of them was employing a young #ZahaHadid.  In 1978, at the peak of his career, he was wrongfully sentenced to life in prison, but was eventually released after 20 months by Saddam Hussein, who was seeking Iraq’s best architect to oversee the preparation of Baghdad for an international conference in 1982.  In 1983 Chadirji eventually fled Baghdad for teaching at Harvard before relocating in the UK where he would spend the rest of his life.  The Burj Abboud survived miraculously six fires, in 1985, 1989, 1996, 1998, 2005 (2x). caption: #Tenerife 🇮🇨 Did you know that the #CanaryIslands were developed on the basis of a genocide?  Before the 15th century Castilian conquest and #colonisation, the islands -located off the coast of present-day Morocco- were inhabited by the Guanches (ⵉⴳⵡⴰⵏⵛⵉⵢⵏ) who were genetically and culturally related to the #Amazigh.  They were descendants of tribes who migrated from North Africa at least 2,000 to 3,000 years ago to develop their own civilisation on the #Canarias. They can be considered the only #AmazighPeople not to have been islamised.   Due to their incredible resistance, brutal fightings with the Spaniards lasted for over a century, but the Guanches people were eventually either killed, raped, enslaved or assimilated. The Canary were hispanized without leaving much space for syncretic culture - as it is often the case in Latin America, for instance. The Guanches’ language, spirituality and culture were forever erased. 💔💔💔  Anyways, thanks for coping with my “architecture post” hacked by some important history context. 🤓  So yeah, here are some 20th-21st architectural gems encountered on the largest and most populous island of the Canary Islands:  1-2: Edificio Cristianmar (residential building), 1960s 3-4: Auditorio de Tenerife Adán Martín (auditorium), designed by architect Santiago Calatrava, built between 1997-2003 5-9: Facultad de Bellas Artes (Universidad La Laguna), designed by Juan Antonio González Pérez, Urbano Yanes Tuña and Constanze Sixt, inaugurated in 2014 10: La iglesia del Santísimo Redentor (church), designed by Menis Arquitectos, built between 2005-2008  #SpanishColonisation #Conquista #arquitectura #archi #archidaily #archilover #modernism #Macaronesia #Espana #Spain #SantaCruzTenerife #LaLagunaTenerife

caption: Eerie vibe in #Varosha, a ghost town turned leisure park   In August 1974, the popular Cypriot beach resort was invaded by the Turkish Army (in the context of the #CyprusProblem). Fearing a massacre, the entire #GreekCypriot population fled the town a few hours earlier.  Emilia (picture 2) was one of them, she now lives in Nicosia: “I was two months pregnant and had three young sons, suddenly we heard that the Turkish Army was attacking by the land and by the sea. Everyone was panicking. We didn’t have time to pack anything, I just took my jewellery. I was a millionaire and within a few minutes I became a refugee, we lost everything. I have nothing against Turkish Cypriots we are just people, the problem is politics.”  The army immediately fenced off the whole area and left it nearly untouched and reclaimed by the nature until this day. 🚧🚧🚧  In October 2020, the #NorthCyprus authorities reopened some streets to visitors. Can’t even imagine what the  Greek Cypriots who have been allowed to visit their town for the first time in 46 years might have felt.  The whole experience is quite weird as the #ghosttown is now equipped like a park. Bikes can be rented and one bar has opened on the beach. I’ve seen many people having a ‘good day out’, taking selfies in front of war leftovers…  According to a U.N. resolution from 1984, only the original inhabitants, who were forced out, could resettle in the town.  In the last few years, the Government of Northern Cyprus has been pushing to normalise the occupation of Varosha ( #Maraş in Turkish) and announced it would open it to settlement. It would imply that if a Greek Cypriot wants to get his building/land back, he would have no other choice than rent a plot to the North Cyprus authorities.  #Famagusta #Mağusa #Gazimağusa #Βαρώσια #ghosttown #DarkTourism #Κύπρος #Kıbrıs #travel #traveler #travelling #traveling #travelers #travels #traveller #traveldeeper #travel#CyprusDispute #CyprusIssue #FacehunterCyprus

caption: #Baghdad - #Iraqi #modernist #architecture ❤️🤍🖤  Roaming around such a major city, that despite how famous it is, I had no idea how it would look like before stepping here. What a feeling!  One type of aesthetics clearly dominates the #urbanscape: contemporary oriental shapes - they are everywhere.  Amazed by how Iraqi modernists worked on abstracting the heritage elements in so many ways.  Baghdad is filled with modernist and #brutalist buildings from the 1960s to 1980s inspired by #IslamicArchitecture (shapes reminiscent of Islamic arches) and occasionally by the volume of ziggurats, these massive Mesopotamian terraced structures.  It’s an old but modern city. More construction took place in Baghdad during the second half of the 20th century than at any time since its foundation in the 8th Century.  After centuries of Ottoman and then British rule; and after deposing its British-backed monarchy in 1958, post-colonial #Iraq -with a growing westernised elite- faced an important question in its urban planning: How would it build a modern nation without sacrificing its national identity?   1: Ministry of Agriculture  2: Al-Mansur neighbourhood  3: Al-Salihiya residential complex, 1984 4: Al-Wathba Square, mural representing Hafidh al-Droubi’s “Watermelon Sellers” (1969) 5: Ministry of Foreign Affairs 6: Central Post, Telegraph and Telephone Administration, 1972 by #RifatChadirji 7: Baghdad Waters Directorate by #HishamMunir & Nasir Al-Asadi, 1978 8: Baghdad City Hall by Hisham Munir & Nasir Al-Asadi, 1975 9: Al-Bataween neighbourhood  10: Ministry of Industry and Minerals by Fadhil Ajina  #facades #brutalism #brutalistarchitecture #archi #baghdadarchitecture #archidaily #architexture #archilovers #baittarkib #visitbaghdad #visitiraq #travel #travelphotography #traveler #travelling #instatravel #traveling #travels #travelholic #FacehunterIraq @traveltoiraq

caption: #Baghdad 🇮🇶 🚴🏽‍♀️ 🎨 Marina @marina_zayed started to ride her #bicycle through the capital of #Iraq in 2016, as an #artproject (during @tarkib_baghdad Festival). Her pictures went viral and inspired many people - men and women - to join her for rides in the city. Marina still organises group bike rides.  “The idea came to me when I first moved out of Baghdad and saw bike rentals. My husband suggested to take a ride and I said I don’t know how to ride a bike. He told me you did it before [as a kid] and it is something you don’t forget. I went on it and it felt so amazing, because it was something I couldn’t do for years. I was told off doing it [as a woman] and when I tried again I felt free and didn’t like the feeling at the same time because I was so proud of myself. I was telling myself, it’s just a bike, I shouldn’t be proud. I didn’t like that my country took that little enjoyment that I had when I was little. I was remembering my grandfather telling me not to, I didn’t understand why, but I followed. It was not even my bike, it was my cousin’s bike, I didn’t have a bike in my life.  The feeling I had that moment, made me want to ride a bike in Baghdad and I thought what’s going to happen. It’s just because people stopped doing things and maybe we should do it again. I bought a bike and brought it all over Baghdad. I remember the first time it was intense, I was so scared. I could hear my heart beats. It felt so amazing. I remember at a checkpoint, I was riding my bike and I was so scared. They wouldn’t tell me off because it’s not illegal but in my head it was something I shouldn’t do. I was riding and I saw him and I was trying to return, I didn’t want him to say anything. What he did, he opened the barrier and let me pass.”  #womenempowerment #womenartists #womanartist #womanpower #artist #baghdadi #baghdad_iraq #baghdadiraq #iraqiartist #iraqipainting #iraqiartists #iraqbaghdad #performanceart #FacehunterIraq

caption: #Nicosia 🧡 looking for hope in the last divided capital.  💞Will love save #Cyprus?💞  “#TurkishCypriots and #GreekCypriots couldn’t meet with each other for decades. But since the checkpoints opened in 2003, people started to fall in love with each other and they were some bi-communal couples. It happens to me as well. A decade ago, it was still something marginal. But now, it has become something more common, it’s part of our daily life, especially for the people of Nicosia.   Unification of the island is our dream, it’s still a long way, it should happen. But first it’s important that we become part of our personal lives, social circles and romantic relationships. Love will save the world!?!  I understand why people think that after many years, a peaceful (but separated) coexistence would be more manageable. But I don’t think Cyprus is big enough for that, especially with bigger problems that we are facing. We have ecosystems being destroyed, we have global warming, we have diminishing resources, we have crisis and violence all around the world, Cyprus is a small small place and it can become an example for a peaceful unification and more democratic ways of living. I guess it’s attainable. It’s just that people got used to think it’s impossible after many years, but it’s not.“ @berandjemal   For nearly a half-century (since 1974), the Republic of Cyprus (🇨🇾) and its capital Nicosia have been split in two and separated by a UN-patrolled buffer zone. caption: Old #Baghdad 🇮🇶 reminiscent of the 1920s to 1960s’ #Iraqi cultural boom.  In their glory, #AlRasheed and #Mutanabi streets used to be home to Baghdad’s intelectual scene and nightlife, with one of the world’s oldest book markets, cinemas (photo 1: Al Zawraa, built in 1936, was one of Iraq’s first cinemas), theatres, and cafés where writers, artists, politicians, intellectuals and students would gather.  After nearly half a century of neglect under Saddam Hussein - who saw the area as a symbol of past rulers and the monarchy - and later during the war,  the historic hub is recently going through a cultural renaissance. Thanks to a better safety situation, many Iraqis from all generations, are being drawn to this spot, to buy books, celebrate their cultural heritage or just hang out. caption: Iraqi-Swedish #artist Sara @saraalmosaibijasas recently had an exhibition (Heal 3.0) and performance @thegallery.iq in #Baghdad  I had the chance to have a coffee with her and chat about identity, art, traumas and moving to Iraq.  "I grew up in Sweden and I came to #Iraq looking for two things: to explore the art scene & to find the piece of my identity that I've always been missing.  I'm not done yet with my quest. I will always be feeling this. When I'm here, I'm not completely home, it feels like home but it is so far away from home. At home, in Sweden, I feel like at home, but there is something missing.  My art show started out as a meditative means for healing my traumas and therapy.  There is a momentum right now in Iraq, things are changing and people feel hope and want to come back to their roots. I have several friends from the diaspora who are considering moving back.  I actually want to move here. I'm trying to arrange that for September.  In Sweden, the streets are clean, life is comfortable, I value that there is a safe system but are they the most important things in my life? The social life, the warmth, the social closeness to my people, my heritage and my language are way more important to me.”  #IraqiArtist #IraqiDiaspora #IraqiWoman #CreativeIraq #Back2TheRoots #IraqiArt #FacehunterIraq 🇮🇶

caption: #Chinguetti 🇲🇷 has always been battling for its own survival against the #Sahara.  In the Middle Age, it managed to become a major cultural, intellectual, religious and trading centre.  For many centuries, the territory of most of present-day #Mauritania was commonly known in the Arab world as Bilad Shinqit, "the land of Chinguetti."  🌙 the “City of Libraries”: in is heyday, it counted up to 30 libraries (for a population of 20,000 people) which housed thousands of Arabic manuscripts, the work of theologians, writers, jurists, philosophers, poets, mathematicians and scientists ranging from the golden age of the Almoravids in Andalusia in the 11th century to the 20th century. Five libraries still remain and I got to visit one: Al-Habot.  🌙 a center of science, religion and mathematics: Mauritanians and other North Western Saharan Islamic scholars have had a profound impact on Islamic culture. Scholars bearing the title al-Shinqiti used to suggest strong scholarly expertise.  🌙 a holy city: the city was a principal gathering place for pilgrims of the Maghreb, on their way to Mecca.  It eventually became known as a holy city in itself, especially for pilgrims who couldn’t make the long journey to the Arabic Peninsula.  🌙 a massive trading-center: desert caravans transporting gold, salt, dates, ivory and… enslaved people across the Sahara were the source of Chinguetti's economic prosperity, with as many as 30,000 camels gathering here at the same time. Historians believe that the spread of Islam is intertwined with the development of the trans-Saharan trade as the religion established common values and a sense of trust among traders.  By the middle of the 19th century, most trans-Saharan commercial arteries dried up, replaced by maritime routes. caption: #Mauritania 🇲🇷 riding the #IronTrain for 20 hours makes you feel slightly delirious… 🌙🪐✨🌞💨  Still trying to process the level of surrealism of sleeping, dreaming and having tea on top of 22,000 tons of iron ore in motion in the middle of the #Sahara.  It is as well a special experience because this 704km-long #railway played an essentiel role in Mauritania’s history.  To exploit a humongous iron ore deposit in the deep desert, a European conglomerate (MiFerMa) created in the 1950s a city from scratch (#Zouerat) and built this #railtrack to carry the raw mineral to the port of Nouadhibou, from where it is exported.  It provided the income for Mauritania's economic development and rapid urbanisation during the first two decades of its independence (1960s-1970s). In 1966, after only three years of operations, iron mining contributed to 28 % of the GDP and accounted for 92% of the value of all exports.  During the Western Sahara War in the 1970s the line became a target of the Polisario Front who partly destroyed it, pushing eventually Mauritania to drop its territorial claim on Western Sahara in 1979. The rail track nowadays briefly crosses the territory of the partially recognized state of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR).  The #DesertTrain plays as well the role of a lifeline for many people and remote desert communities who need to travel to visit family or search for work. There is one passenger carriage at the very end of the world’s longest (2-3km) and heaviest train, but most people ride it atop the iron ore. caption: A Golden Night. Oh, what a night!   Seeing so many of us celebrating and rooting for each other with so much love, respect, and reverence was emotional. For decades we have either downplayed or have never been given any platform to share our incredible stories. We fought for it, demanded it and eventually, when they felt a little "generous", they gave us the crumbs. We saw that and built Gold House. We made our table a decision-making and celebratory one. We created a community that rooted and showed up for each other. We took the trauma, pain of invisibility and turned it into action. The result is there for you all to see.   What astounds me is that it's just the 2nd annual #GoldGala and less than four years of Gold House's existence, and the impact is quantifiable and inspiring thanks to the incredible leadership of @BingChen and JeremyNTran.  You had to be there to witness the collective love of and from the community and beyond. To see the entire cast of Joy Luck Club celebrated was very emotional. The impactful joy that Gold House brings could be felt throughout–titans of every industry, from entertainment to business to technology to politics to social justice, attended. Allies from other communities equally rejoicing in our celebration felt like I was finally in a dream I had dreamt all these years. A table and space so diverse that my life's " stronger in colour" mantra finally manifested into a reality. It was palpable not just to me but to everyone out there. Celebration with intention creates change, and the entire Gold House team created a substantive, celebratory gala that I will forever remember.  As Instyle rightfully said, "You may not have realised it, but last week was host to not one but two major Galas." The Met Gala and Gold Gala."  Luckily I had the privilege to attend both and walked away from them feeling inspired and energised because witnessing the body of work of all these creatives, artists, entrepreneurs etc., celebrated and in attendance was inspiring and humbling.   I realise now I have miles to go before I sleep.

caption: Planta que cresce em roupa? Foi isso mesmo que vimos no desfile da marca @martins__________  em uma colaboração com a designer espanhola Paula Ulargui (@ulargui_escalona ) e a @oficialype   Paula tem um projeto incrível que tem chamado atenção de marcas do mundo inteiro. Foi seu trabalho do último ano da faculdade e que tem rendido reflexões sobre nossa relação com a natureza e da própria indústria da moda com o meio ambiente.  A roupa é feita com um material de fibras naturais que proporcionam o ambiente perfeito pra planta crescer dentro do tecido, com os nutrientes certos. Alguns tecidos são mais fáceis de implementar as sementes, outros exigem mais técnica.  E o mais surpreendente é que Paula mostrou que isso é possível: plantas crescendo em roupas. E que o cuidado é fundamental para que elas durem e você possa continuar usando. Isso também traz muitas reflexões acerca da nossa relação com a “Fico feliz que um projeto tão pessoal pra mim tem se transformado numa nova maneira da gente conectar com a natureza. O projeto tem recebido uma repercussão enorme e tenho trabalhado em colab com diversas marcas pelo mundo. E fiquei muito contente de vir para o Brasil trabalhar com a equipe do Tom e da Ypê”, finaliza Paula. caption: @maisonvalentino presents the Fall/Winter 2023-24 collection, Creative Director Pierpaolo Piccioli takes black tie at its face value, a figure of speech for a collection centered on garments drawn from the everyday. Conjectures and cultural capital are reversed: symbol of male power, emblem of orthodoxy and restriction, our preconceptions about the tie become theoretical architecture for a collection that plays with rules, emancipating meaning. Its ideological conception is questioned, eventually contradicted and completely redefined.  The conscious journey of Maison Valentino continues in its constant commitment to greater environmental awareness also on the occasion of the Valentino Black Tie Fall/Winter 2023 fashion show.   The guests of the show are hosted on wooden benches that will be entirely reused by the Maison for its future events and projects, with a view to supporting the reuse of resources. The carpet is totally recycled following the event by its Italian supplier, equally attentive to the environmental impact and characterized by eco-conscious ethics. The brand will donate part of the textile materials used for the fashion show to the association with the aim of promoting the circular economy. #CNMIMembers #ValentinoBlackTie #MaisonValentino

caption: #Casablanca 🇲🇦 was one of the most important #architectural laboratories in the 20th Century and it still shows. Can’t remember last time I’ve seen as many unique expressions of #modernism. There are literally not two identical #buildings in #Morocco‘s economic capital.  After almost entirely destroying Casablanca and killing 7,000 people in 1907, France decided to build a “ville nouvelle” (new city) for its large European population and a “ville indigène” (Indigineous city) to house Moroccans.  During its rule of Morocco (1912-1956), France invited European architects to use Casa as their canva. It turned into what has been considered “a model of a modernist city”. caption: Midnights is a wild ride of an album and I couldn’t be happier that my co pilot on this adventure was @jackantonoff. He’s my friend for life (presumptuous I know but I stand by it) and we’ve been making music together for nearly a decade HOWEVER… this is our first album we’ve done with just the two of us as main collaborators. We’d been toying with ideas and had written a few things we loved, but Midnights actually really coalesced and flowed out of us when our partners (both actors) did a film together in Panama. Jack and I found ourselves back in New York, alone, recording every night, staying up late and exploring old memories and midnights past. We were so lucky to also work with our brilliant collaborators @sam_dew, @sounwave, Lana Del Rey, @jahaansweet, @keanubeats, William Bowery, and @zoeisabellakravitz. @sharp_stick was our excellent engineer. The wonderful and wise @bethgarrabrant took the album photographs. Midnights is a collage of intensity, highs and lows and ebbs and flows. Life can be dark, starry, cloudy, terrifying, electrifying, hot, cold, romantic or lonely. Just like Midnights. Which is out now

caption: ⴷⴷⴰⵅⵍⴰ 🇪🇭 #Dakhla, where the Atlantic meets the #Sahara, is at the heart of Morocco's colonial startegy to anchor its presence in the disputed territory of #WesternSahara.  While all Moroccan public services function in Dakhla as they would in any other part of Morocco proper, international laws consider that (most of) WS is occupied by Morocco.  In the last decades, Morocco has invested millions to transform a modest and remote, fishing village into a major Saharan economic and tourism hub.  The new eldorado (?) attracts many Moroccans and sub-Saharian people looking for opportunities. The city counts nowadays over 100,000 inhabitants. Recently, Dakhla has also emerged as a popular destination for kite-surfers. Is the growing number of Western tourists helping to erase appearances of an ongoing geopolitical dispute?  The Kingdom will keep investing on mega-projects, such as the creation of the "biggest port in Morocco" when completed in 2030 and a leisure port to attract cruise ships and connect Dakhla to the nearby Canary Islands by ferry.  These heavy developments geopardise more than ever the chances of self-determination for the #Sahrawi people (the ethnic group native to the western part of the Sahara).  #dakhlacity #dakhlah #dakhlaspirit #dakhlah #occupation #colonisation #colonialism #SaharaOccidental #NorthAfrica #AfriqueduNord #westernsaharaconflict

caption: The #CuronianSpit 🇱🇹 a miraculous 98km-long sand dune peninsula connecting #Lithuania and Russia. Before coming here, I didn’t know that such a place could exist.  Depending if you are more into mythology or geology, the #sandspit was created by Neringa, a good-hearted giantess to protect her coastline from an evil dragon or by the combined action of the sea, wind and human activity over the last 5,000 years.  Nevertheless, the existence of this “ephemeral territory” is constantly under threat, it would take very little to have it vanish completely.  After intensive logging in the 17th and 18th centuries, the dunes began moving very fast and buried entire towns, including #Nida (#Nidden back then) the main settlement. From the 19th century onwards, tree planting, creation of a protective dune ridge along the seashore and limitation of public access have contributed to “stabilise” the Spit.   Nida, is the last Lithuanian town, just 3km before the Russian border. There is something quite odd about the contrast between such a peaceful-looking family-friendly holiday destination dotted with 19th century wooden fisherman’s houses and the tension of the war involving the big neighbour.   This coastal region has been the home of Baltic and Germanic cultures for many centuries. With its incorporation in the German Empire in the late 19th century, Nida became a Summer hotspot for German artists and intellectuals.  Have you been here or would you consider visiting?  #KuršiųNerija #Куршскаякоса #Baltic #Baltics #BalticState #BalticStates #Lietuva #BaltijosJūra #FacehunterLT

caption: #Accra 🇬🇭 post-independence #architecture 🏗️  When #Ghana gained independence from Britain in 1957, first president, Kwame Nkrumah used the modernist architectural language to express the Ghanaian identity and project its new aspirations.  Inheriting a state with very few home-grown architects and planners, Nkrumah, the “socialist scientist”, created alliances with “Eastern Bloc” states and hired talents from Poland, Bulgaria, Yugoslavia, East Germany and Soviet Union to build the new Ghana.  Poland occupied a central role in this, 26 Polish architects worked at the Ghana National Construction Corporation (GNCC) during the 1960s, on projects in the capital. For instance, the Labadi neighbourhood in #Accra was planned based on the post-war remodelling of a Warsaw district (Powiśle).   In short span of time, tons of civic buildings were commissioned by the government : schools, libraries, universities and hospitals. The East European architects often tried to adapt the international #modernist style to Ghanian culture and tropical climate. Some called this sub-genre: #TropicalModernism.  The “architecture of independence” shows the contradictions and challenges in Ghana’s nation building and independence process. caption: 💚💛❤️ #Architecture in #Nouakchott, the capital of #Mauritania 🇲🇷  🔺🔳🔶🔹🔸🔷🔳🔺 #SaharanModernism  Before becoming the capital of then newly independent Mauritania in 1960, #NKT was just a small fisherman’s town, located between the Atlantic Ocean and the #Sahara.  It counts now nearly 2 million beating hearts. Over the decades, multiple droughts forced subsistence farmers and nomadic people from across the country into #NKTT.   The original village was selected as the capital city for its central location meant to avoid the sensitive issue of whether it was built in an area dominated by the Arab-descended Moors or Subsaharan Africans.  Nouakchott means “Place of the Winds” in Amazigh language and it actually makes sense as the winds are pushing sand dunes into the city. Creating an important challenge for the capital’s future.  #Sahara #Sahel #Modernism #Modernist #DesertArchitecture #architecture #archi #archidaily #archilover #archilovers #archiporn #africanmodernism #africanbrutalism #Mauritanie #FacehunterMauritania

caption: 5 years ago I have created 'Date With Versace' and my life has changed since.   Words can not describe my feelings about this page. It's more than an Instagram account, it became an integral part of my life. There were so many good and bad days, but all of them started with 'Date With Versace'.  What if... what if I didn't even started the DWV?  I don't even want to think about it.  5 years ago, I was a little girl - confused, with the big dreams and passion for the fashion and now I'm the part of this industry. Exactly this page helped me to understand that I want to work in Fashion.  Little me wouldn’t even believe the realness of the past 5 years. Still feels like a dream.  I'm so thankful to all the employees of Versace, who are always there to help and take care of me. Although some of them are no longer working in the brand, I want you to remember that you are always in my heart and I will never forget what you have done for me.  I'm happiest that my journey is inspirational for the young talents, who really want to work in this industry and do not know from where to start. My story is a sign that everything is possible.   I believe with all my heart that the best is yet to come!   And... This wouldn’t have been possible without your support. THANK YOU for your love!  Keti   @datewithversace @versace @donatella_versace #Versace #DateWithVersace #DonatellaVersace
